ClientResponses.Response:
We appreciate your feedback. We are so sorry to hear about the grill not fully heating up. We are happy to help. It sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. Follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is also the way you would want to start your grill each and every time.

1. Open the lid
2. Make sure all knobs are in the off position (including side burner if applicable)
3. Turn your LP tank on all the way
4. Wait 30-60 seconds
5. Turn the first burner to start/high (first position to the left)
6. Hit your igniter
7. Turn on all remaining burners
8. Close the lid to preheat to 500-550°F

Hopefully, this information helps you get back up and running smoothly again. 

Our Care team will be reaching out to follow up. Thank you!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber grills

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
There are quality control problems at Weber. First, they shipped a major component that made assembly impossible. Next, the regulator failed almost immediately and blocked the gas transmission to the grill. There's an indication of a design defect in the warning to open the source gas tank very slowly so the regulator doesn't lock up. That tells us that they've run into a lot of regulator problems and that they haven't engineered the mechanism right. Nothing should be that sensitive. (I have a degree in mechanical engineering, and worked in the field for a number of years, so I have some history of dealing with mechanical designing.) They know that the regulator is underdesigned, and they're trying to pass the issue onto the consumer. Presumably, in time, they'll redesign the regulator to work properly and not fail so easily.
       On the positive side, the customer support was largely very responsive. They replaced the incorrect part (It took 6 days to arrive), and they didn't dispute my recognition that the regulator was at fault for the grill not working. Again, they promptly replaced the regulator (taking 4 or 5 days). The only fault I found with customer support was that neither of the agents knew enough to say, "We're sorry that you're having a problem." That magic word, 'sorry,' helps a lot, and it's clear that the agents haven't been trained to acknowledge that their mistakes have inconvenienced a customer. The prompt resolutions certainly helped, as did the positive attitudes, but it never hurts to accept responsibility AND apologize for it.
Results.Title: Quality Control Issues/Prompt Resolution
